hypothesis: The parent's density relaxation is gated only on global overflow and worst-region density, but the TNS/WNS cost comes from *timing-critical* cells being pushed into dense regions; make the early quadratic ramp of the density weight start later (longer window) and additionally keep a slightly higher floor on `mu` when HPWL is improving, so the placer spends more iterations in the wirelength-friendly regime where critical nets stay short, reducing TNS.
expected_effect: TNS improves (positive), WNS slightly improves, overflow unchanged or slightly lower, runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with TNS gains (+19–28%) exceeding WNS gains, consistent with keeping critical nets short during the wirelength-friendly regime. bp-ng45 showed the largest WNS move (+17.4%), suggesting the delayed density ramp most helped its timing-critical cells. Overflow stayed ~110–145, so no legality cost. Next step: sweep the ramp-start offset and `mu` floor jointly on bp-ng45 to find whether the WNS gain saturates before overflow degrades, confirming the mechanism rather than a single lucky setting.
